tooling.reason: Kept apart from the guidance commit that follows it: a code fix of the publish action, not guidance.
tooling.message:
fix(publish): deploy even when Pages is off, fail only after the deploy

## Intent

When Pages was off or misconfigured, the publish action stopped before the deploy. After the creator's click Pages served the old state, and the integration may not start a rerun (403), so the agent pushed a dummy change to trigger one. The creator's click should show the newest state at once.

## Key changes

- A Pages setup the token may not fix is a warning before the deploy; the check after the deploy fails until the creator makes the click. The message says that no new run is needed.
- The advice to set the default branch uses REST (`gh api -X PATCH repos/<o>/<r> -f default_branch=main`), since GraphQL may be blocked where the assistant runs.

## Dependencies and side effects

- `publish.ts before` exits 0 on a wrong Pages setup; its tests expect the warning and the failure of `after`.
- Part of making the GitHub side transparent, with 9cf04cd and lernapps/apps ba3d7e7 (same intent).

tooling.message:
feat(guidance): make the GitHub side transparent from the start

## Intent

The first full creator run lost most time on GitHub: work became the default branch, Pages was off at the first deploy, GraphQL was blocked, a rename cost access, and an early message was taken as a yes. The tooling works deeply with GitHub. Creators should know what that means without having to know GitHub, and agents should set it up right at the start.

## Key changes

- In Explore the agent tells the creator where the app lives (own repo, GitHub Pages, public, free) and offers to explain GitHub in plain words. A new docs page, https://lernapps.net/tooling/github/, explains it for humans.
- The agent fixes the repo name, pushes main alone so it becomes the default branch, then creates gh-pages and work and sets the Pages source, before anything else is pushed. The Commit phase only verifies and brings work into main by fast-forward.
- New compact skill lernapps-github: tool order (gh over REST, then MCP, then curl), GraphQL may be blocked, "403 by integration" means a click for the creator and never a dummy push, REST checks, and the listing pull request from a fork.
- stop-at-checkpoints: a message sent before the checkpoint question is not a yes.
- lernapps-interactive: how to handle the frame and a full-screen game (overlay, way out, focus, keys that scroll the page).

## Dependencies and side effects

- A new guidance test checks the branch setup in Explore and that the template has no GraphQL `gh repo` commands.
- AGENTS.md is at its word limit, so it does not reference the new skill.
- dcf5561 changes the publish action; lernapps/apps ba3d7e7 links the new page and writes out the fork path (same intent).

apps.message:
docs: explain GitHub to creators, the fork path, and review the head of main

## Intent

In the first creator run the review read a stale work, the default branch, and failed the plan. The listing path did not say to use a fork, so the way real creators must take stayed untested. Creators also need a plain word that the app lives on GitHub and that they need not know it.

## Key changes

- `/review` without a commit reads the head of main (else HEAD), says which ref it read, and warns when the default branch is not main.
- llms.txt writes out the fork path and points to the new tooling skill lernapps-github.
- The build page links the tooling's page "GitHub, explained".

## Dependencies and side effects

- The review comment's closing line changed; the golden comment follows.
- Needs lernapps/tooling 9cf04cd (same intent) for the linked page and skill.
